test_modes.name: Register read/write
test_modes.purpose: Exercise ID0/ID1 and CR0/CR1 access in the register address space.

test_modes.name: Latency sweep
test_modes.purpose: Validate each configurable initial-latency code (3..7) at the target frequency.

test_modes.name: Burst type / length
test_modes.purpose: Exercise wrapped, linear, and hybrid bursts at each configured length.

test_modes.name: Deep power down (HyperRAM)
test_modes.purpose: Enter DPD via CR0 and verify wake-up timing.

spec_provided_observability.name: Identification Registers (ID0/ID1)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Read-only manufacturer/device ID, row/column address bit counts, and device size — used to discover and validate the attached device.

spec_provided_observability.name: Configuration Registers (CR0/CR1)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Read back the configured latency, latency model, drive strength, burst length, and refresh control to confirm host programming.

spec_provided_observability.name: RWDS during CA
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Observe the variable-latency 1x/2x indication for timing bring-up.

spec_provided_observability.name: RWDS read strobe
spec_provided_observability.purpose: The edge-aligned read strobe is the key signal-integrity / timing observable during read bring-up.

error_detection_mechanisms: Read-back of ID/Configuration registers verifies device presence and host programming.
RWDS strobe alignment confirms DDR read capture timing.
Drive-strength adjustment (CR0) addresses board signal-integrity failures.

interrupt_or_event_sources.trigger: RWDS asserted during the CA phase.

notes: HyperBus's protocol-level test surface is the ID/Configuration register space plus the RWDS strobe behaviour (variable-latency indication and read-data strobe). Chip-level JTAG/scan/BIST remain controller / SoC-integrator concerns.
